CONSTRUCT appears to have been implemented for Mulgara 2.0.0:

The exception message from Trippi is misleading, from what I can see in the 1.4.1 source.  MulgaraSession#findTriples(String lang, String queryText) is unimplemented; SPO queries are the only ones that apear to be processed at all.  This is also indicated in the single value of MulgaraSessionFactory/TRIPLE_LANGUAGES: "spo".
The triple query aspect of the report is a Trippi issue, though finding a way for the risearch stylesheet to suppress non-SPO triple query options would be good in the meantime.
RE: The tuples aspect: the query is successful with a from clause:
It would probably also work if <#ri> were passed in as the value of the "default-graph-uri" parameter to the Mulgara servlet; I'll try to test that later, but I think this is a minor issue.
EDIT: Scratch that, that's from the Mulgara REST api, not Trippi.  The short answer is just to include the from clause.
Working on Sparql triple support in the Mulgara connector, most of this will probably be in the Trippi codebase.

That branch adds support for Sparql triple queries to the Mulgara connector, and makes use of default graph uri's.  It passes integration tests (and preliminary desktop testing).  I'll request a review next week, but you should be able to build a drop-in replacement for Fedora's trippi jars in a pinch.
Overall looks good. Thanks for taking this on. Couple points:
1) What was the reason for overriding count() in MulgaraTupleIterator and MulgaraTripleIterator? CollapsedAnswer.getRowCount always throws an exception.

2) When I saw you cutting & pasting existing code for substituting <# for <m_serverURI in MulgaraSession, I was originally going to suggest pulling that out into a private function or possibly into doAliasReplacements, but actually, I think the whole substitution is unnecessary. Moreover it's incomplete: it's case sensitive, so something like FROM <#foo> won't get subbed out. It doesn't matter because Mulgara takes <#foo> just fine without our substitution. Not sure if this is something that has changed in Mulgara or we've just been doing unnecessarily all along. So I think you can safely pull it out of you updates (and we can see about cleaning up the rest at another point).
Re point 2, the graph URI substition, this is a change in Mulgara - relative graph URIs such as <#model> will now work, there's no need to substitute for the full URI (versions 2.0.9 and 2.1.0)

1) In a local trippi, my testing showed the Mulgara count to be faster (and I needed faster counts on big-ish result sets), but I merged the two changes incorrectly.  I'll fix it, and add an integration test for  count later today.

EDIT: And the relative speed of the count technique is irrelevant if it never gets called.  The MulgaraTupleIterator is more heavily decorated than I expected.  I'll yank the count methods on the next rev.
2) Point well taken.  When I update the tests, I'll make sure that relative uris are tested as well.

branch rev 120 consolidates the base model substitutions into doAliasReplacements, removes the irrelevant count overrides, and adds a little test coverage.  On my development machine, Mulgara choked on IRIs like <#ri-test>: It tried to append them to default URIs, got a result string that had two hashes, and threw an exception trying to make a URI from it.  When I tried removing the hash, mulgara attempted to load a Jena class to parse the resulting RDF.  I decided the easiest way was to preserver the general logic of the existing substitution, with a slightly more flexible pattern match.

I'll look into the graph uri substitution again after I update Mulgara. Thanks in particular for fleshing out the test case. Everything looks good to me so I say you should go ahead w/ merging with trunk.

comments.body: verified w/paul that construct is supported in mulgara

CONSTRUCT appears to have been implemented for Mulgara 2.0.0:
http://www.mulgara.org/trac/ticket/112

The exception message from Trippi is misleading, from what I can see in the 1.4.1 source. MulgaraSession#findTriples(String lang, String queryText) is unimplemented; SPO queries are the only ones that apear to be processed at all. This is also indicated in the single value of MulgaraSessionFactory/TRIPLE_LANGUAGES: "spo".

The triple query aspect of the report is a Trippi issue, though finding a way for the risearch stylesheet to suppress non-SPO triple query options would be good in the meantime.

RE: The tuples aspect: the query is successful with a from clause:
construct

{ ?x <dc:title> ?name }

from <#ri> where

{ ?x <dc:identifier> ?name }

It would probably also work if <#ri> were passed in as the value of the "default-graph-uri" parameter to the Mulgara servlet; I'll try to test that later, but I think this is a minor issue.

EDIT: Scratch that, that's from the Mulgara REST api, not Trippi. The short answer is just to include the from clause.
Working on Sparql triple support in the Mulgara connector, most of this will probably be in the Trippi codebase.

https://trippi.svn.sourceforge.net/svnroot/trippi/branches/FCREPO-478

That branch adds support for Sparql triple queries to the Mulgara connector, and makes use of default graph uri's. It passes integration tests (and preliminary desktop testing). I'll request a review next week, but you should be able to build a drop-in replacement for Fedora's trippi jars in a pinch.

Ben,

Overall looks good. Thanks for taking this on. Couple points:

1) What was the reason for overriding count() in MulgaraTupleIterator and MulgaraTripleIterator? CollapsedAnswer.getRowCount always throws an exception.

2) When I saw you cutting & pasting existing code for substituting <# for <m_serverURI in MulgaraSession, I was originally going to suggest pulling that out into a private function or possibly into doAliasReplacements, but actually, I think the whole substitution is unnecessary. Moreover it's incomplete: it's case sensitive, so something like FROM <#foo> won't get subbed out. It doesn't matter because Mulgara takes <#foo> just fine without our substitution. Not sure if this is something that has changed in Mulgara or we've just been doing unnecessarily all along. So I think you can safely pull it out of you updates (and we can see about cleaning up the rest at another point).

Eddie

Re point 2, the graph URI substition, this is a change in Mulgara - relative graph URIs such as <#model> will now work, there's no need to substitute for the full URI (versions 2.0.9 and 2.1.0)

Eddie:
Thanks for checking it out.

1) In a local trippi, my testing showed the Mulgara count to be faster (and I needed faster counts on big-ish result sets), but I merged the two changes incorrectly. I'll fix it, and add an integration test for count later today.

EDIT: And the relative speed of the count technique is irrelevant if it never gets called. The MulgaraTupleIterator is more heavily decorated than I expected. I'll yank the count methods on the next rev.

2) Point well taken. When I update the tests, I'll make sure that relative uris are tested as well.

FCREPO-478 Closed branch rev 120 consolidates the base model substitutions into doAliasReplacements, removes the irrelevant count overrides, and adds a little test coverage. On my development machine, Mulgara choked on IRIs like <#ri-test>: It tried to append them to default URIs, got a result string that had two hashes, and threw an exception trying to make a URI from it. When I tried removing the hash, mulgara attempted to load a Jena class to parse the resulting RDF. I decided the easiest way was to preserver the general logic of the existing substitution, with a slightly more flexible pattern match.

I'll look into the graph uri substitution again after I update Mulgara. Thanks in particular for fleshing out the test case. Everything looks good to me so I say you should go ahead w/ merging with trunk.
Will close this after updating Mulgara to 2.1.4 (see FCREPO-580 Closed )

Issuing a SPARQL query for a CONSTRUCT results in an empty response from the tuple query type service and a Exception is thrown when attempting to use the triples query service:

(Via Tuples
e.g. http://databank.ouls.ox.ac.uk:8080/fedora/risearch?lang=sparql&format=sparql&type=tuples&query=construct%20

{%20?x%20dc:title%20?name%20}

%20WHERE%20

{%20?x%20dc:title%20?name%20}

SPARQL query:

CONSTRUCT

{ ?x dc:title ?title }

WHERE

{ ?x dc:title ?title }

[' make a graph of all triples with dc:title as a predicate.']

Response:
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<sparql xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2001/sw/DataAccess/rf1/result">
<head>
<variable name="subject"/>
<variable name="predicate"/>
<variable name="object"/>
</head>
<results>
</results>
</sparql>

(regardless to how many dc:title triples are there: e.g. an spo query to pull up 10 dc:title matches - http://databank.ouls.ox.ac.uk:8080/fedora/risearch?lang=spo&format=RDF/XML&type=triples&limit=10&query=*%20%3Cdc:title%3E%20* )

(Via Triples
http://databank.ouls.ox.ac.uk:8080/fedora/risearch?lang=sparql&format=sparql&type=triples&query=construct%20
